comparator.name: Bachelor Theology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page, 2026-2027 study guide, course overview and OER identify a three-year, 180-EC Bachelor Theology offered full-time or part-time. The standard full-time curriculum builds from Bible, systematic theology, religious studies, practical theology, church history, ethics, philosophy, intercultural theology and sustained biblical Hebrew and New Testament Greek into advanced exegesis, hermeneutics, missiology, church practice, professional formation and a 10-EC Bachelor thesis. The third year preserves 30 EC of genuine internal or external minor space. The 2026-2027 guide states that the former Religion and Society Track 2 was converted from September 2026 into the third-year Theology for Church and Society minor/variant; it is therefore not treated as a continuing formal route for this generic normalized target.

components.name: Year 1: theology, Bible and biblical-language foundations
components.note: Theology for church and world, systematic theology, religious studies, practical theology, Old and New Testament study, church history, ethics, philosophy, intercultural theology, biblical Hebrew, New Testament Greek, and personal and professional formation.

components.name: Year 2: exegesis, hermeneutics and theological progression
components.note: Systematic theology, philosophical anthropology, psychology of religion, philosophical hermeneutics, Old and New Testament study, exegetical methods, practical theology, missiology, church history, continuing biblical Hebrew and Greek, and personal and professional formation.

components.name: Year 3: minor space, advanced theology and Bachelor thesis
components.note: Thirty EC of genuine internal or external minor space, plus ethics and spirituality, practical theology, continuing biblical Hebrew and Greek, personal and professional formation, the relationship between Old and New Testaments, and the 10-EC Bachelor thesis.

programmes.label: Bachelor Theology at Theological University Utrecht

exception.reason: The TU Utrecht Bachelor Theology is a cumulative academic theology degree whose required formation combines Bible and Old and New Testament study, sustained biblical Hebrew and New Testament Greek, systematic theology, religious studies, church history, ethics, philosophy, hermeneutics, exegetical methods, practical theology, missiology, spiritual and professional formation, and a theology-specific Bachelor thesis. Even with 30 EC of minor space, the programme's remaining 150 EC retain a dense theological, biblical, linguistic and church-practice core. UCR offers adjacent work in philosophy, ethics, history, literature, rhetoric, sociology, politics and cultural study, but no theology or religious-studies curriculum, biblical-language or exegesis sequence, or practical-theology formation. A 24-course UCR pathway could address religion as one historical, philosophical or social phenomenon, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as Theology.
exception.curriculumContext: The current full-time curriculum totals 180 EC: 60 EC in each of three years. Year 1 establishes theology, biblical study, religious studies, church history, ethics, philosophy, practical and intercultural theology, biblical Hebrew and New Testament Greek. Year 2 advances systematic theology, Old and New Testament study, exegetical methods, hermeneutics, psychology of religion, missiology, practical theology, church history and both biblical languages. Year 3 combines 30 EC of genuine minor space with advanced ethics and spirituality, practical theology, further Hebrew and Greek, professional formation, the relationship between the Old and New Testaments and a 10-EC Bachelor thesis. The 2026-2027 study guide explicitly records that the former 35-EC Religion and Society Track 2 was converted from September 2026 into a third-year minor/variant, so the current ordinary theology curriculum is the appropriate neutral reconstruction for the generic target.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, GOSPHIL212 Ethics, GOSPOLI111 Introduction to Political Philosophy and GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy support philosophical and moral inquiry. GOSHIST111 Modern History and the wider history sequence provide historical methods; MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature support literary and mythological interpretation; MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication supports rhetorical analysis; and sociology and politics courses can examine religion's social and public contexts indirectly. The workbook nevertheless contains no theology or religious-studies course, Old or New Testament study, biblical exegesis, scriptural hermeneutics, biblical Hebrew or New Testament Greek, systematic theology, church history as a disciplinary sequence, missiology, ecclesiology, practical theology, worship, pastoral formation, or theology-specific Bachelor research project. The available adjacent humanities and social-science courses cannot supply the connected 150-EC theological, biblical, linguistic and practice-oriented core that remains after the comparator's genuine 30-EC minor space is preserved.
